headline: Growth slows, margins widen amid heavy buybacks
summary_short: ZoomInfo's Q1 2026 revenue rose 1.5% y/y to $310.2M but slipped 2.8% q/q, with net revenue retention improving to 90% from 87% a year ago even as diluted EPS held at $0.10, down from $0.11 the prior quarter.
summary_long: Revenue grew 1.5% y/y to $310.2M as continued upmarket mix shift and improving net revenue retention (90% vs 87% y/y) offset a 2.8% sequential pullback. Gross margin slipped to 84% (from 85% y/y) as hosting/infrastructure and depreciation costs outpaced revenue growth, though gross profit dollars were roughly flat. Operating income rose 15% y/y to $57.9M on lower compensation and equity-based compensation costs, lifting operating margin to 19% from 16%; net income rose 9% y/y to $29.3M despite higher interest expense and a higher 33.9% effective tax rate. The company repurchased $90.5M of stock this quarter, pulling cash to $171.2M and equity to $1,473.6M, both down q/q. This 10-Q discloses no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects the continued shift of the business mix upmarket and the resulting improvement in net revenue retention (90% vs 87% a year ago), partly offset by normal quarterly seasonality in renewals and invoice timing.

Dollars were roughly flat as higher revenue was mostly offset by higher hosting/infrastructure expense and capitalized-software depreciation, partly offset by lower amortization of fully-amortized acquired technology; gross margin fell to 84% from 85% y/y.

Rose on higher revenue, lower employee compensation and equity-based compensation expense, and lower acquired-technology amortization, partly offset by lease/leasehold-impairment charges and higher hosting and technology expense.
Tracked the operating-income gain, partially offset by higher interest expense (lower interest income from derivative swaps) and a higher 33.9% effective tax rate (vs 32.2% y/y).
Grew faster than net income as diluted weighted-average shares fell to 302.5M from 340.7M a year earlier, reflecting continued buybacks ($90.5M repurchased this quarter).

Fell as $90.9M of stock buybacks, $1.5M of debt repayment, and $0.8M of share-settlement tax payments in financing activities outpaced $114.7M of operating cash flow against $26.0M of net investing outflows.
Fell q/q and y/y as $90.5M of quarterly share buybacks reduced paid-in capital and retained earnings faster than net income added to them.

MD&A frames the quarter as steady upmarket-driven growth and net-revenue-retention improvement funding operating-leverage gains, alongside continued heavy buybacks under the $2.6B authorization ($1.14B remaining as of quarter-end).
